question.problem: Given that $f(x)=4{e}^{x}+17$, the slope of the tangent line at $x=\operatorname{ln}⁡3$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The derivative of ${e}^{x}$ is just ${e}^{x}$ itself. On the other hand, $17$ is a constant, so its derivative is $0.$

First, using the addition rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{e}^{x}+17) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{e}^{x})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(17) \\  & =4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x})+0 \\  & =4{e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=\operatorname{ln}⁡3$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=\operatorname{ln}⁡3} & ={(4{e}^{x})\,|}_{x=\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =4{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\  & =4\cdot 3 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$
